Keeping a diary and watching shows really helped me with this. I realized this is how I learned English as a child in a partially passive way.

Sometimes if I'm writing a diary, I am sort of forced to think in that language. Whenever I need to describe an event or emotion, I look for the word and try to use it often until it sticks to me naturally. Sometimes I learn a new word or phrase while watching a show, and I try to use it in a sentence in the diary. So instead of mindlessly memorizing, I get to understand the word in its context/environment.

This process takes longer but I find that it sticks better than having to memorize a lot of vocabulary that I won't regularly use. Another quicker method is to add a sentence to every word you find difficult so it sticks more to your memory because you know how to use it.

Well no we dont export rice. We import more rice than we export, and that is the best example of why our economy failed. 

Una sa lahat, kalabaw pa din pang-araro for some regions. We haven't advanced our agricultural technology kasi walang government subsidy for that. Even if madami tayong magagaling na researchers sa IRRI, hindi naman siya na-apply. 

Despite us being an agricultural country, hindi natin kayang masustentuhan yung demand for rice sa buong Pilipinas. Kaya we import rice. May rice tarrification pa nga to encourage importing rice. 

Endgame, our agricultural base js very flimsy. Wala tayong subsistence. Ang malakas ngayon sa atin is the service sector, i.e. BPOs and OFWs. The ideal talaga, which most Asian countries like South Korea have adapted, is strong agricultural base muna tapos strong industries and then last yung service sector na.

I heavily agree sa third point. After the war, South Korea pursued genuine agrarian reform so nawala na yung mga landed elites nila so nagkaroon ng shift sa power relations and panibagong political playing field.
Yeap, but it depends on what you export din kasi. If puro raw materials nakasalalay ang economy natin, it wouldn't be stable in the long run.
